title: Tennis Surface Transfer
headline_insight: The most extreme clay-over-hard specialist in the ATP career snapshot is Luciano Darderi, a 0.4603 clay-minus-hard win-rate gap, 0.6825 on clay against 0.2222 on hard.
what_it_means: Surface specialization is real and large for a few players but modest for most: across the 184 qualifying ATP-career players the median clay-minus-hard gap is only +0.0149, and 58.15% tilt at all toward clay. The women's combos are empty here, the sample-size floor eliminated every WTA player.
how_to_read: Each player's clay win rate minus hard win rate (and a grass-adaptability index), floored at 25 clay and 25 hard matches, summarized per tour and window.
why_it_matters: It is a descriptive map of who actually transfers between surfaces, the raw split behind any surface-aware reasoning.
caveat: Opponent strength is NOT controlled, so a gap partly reflects scheduling and seeding rather than surface skill alone; retirements count as decided matches; DESCRIPTIVE_ONLY, no forecast and no market or ROI edge.
as_of: tennis_surface_context snapshots (no generation timestamp in artifact)
